title: The Collapsing Mine
logline: An unstable asteroid mine collapses, and a union organiser begs a pilot to buy and deliver structural supports because the company refuses to halt operations.

roles.description: Exhausted, hoarse from shouting, deeply protective of their crew.
Cold, numbers-driven, refuses to acknowledge danger.
A hollowed-out rock groaning under gravitational stress.
A pristine office overlooking the dirty asteroid.
A massive conglomerate focused purely on quotas.

public_situation: The {role:mining_corporation} has doubled production quotas at the {role:unstable_asteroid}, ignoring reports of structural fatigue.
private_truth: The company knows the asteroid will collapse. They increased quotas to extract all the ore before the inevitable disaster, writing off the miners as an insurance loss.

beats.public_change: A minor cave-in traps three miners, and the company docks their pay for the lost time.

missions.reason: The organiser begs the pilot to buy heavy titanium struts and deliver them to the mine.
missions.private_fact: The miners are installing the struts themselves off the clock just to survive their shifts.

beats.public_change: The company issues a memo declaring the mine officially safe.

missions.reason: The bureaucrat hires the pilot to run a superficial sensor sweep to certify the rock is stable.
missions.private_fact: The pilot's deep scan reveals the rock's core is fracturing and will collapse in less than a day.

beats.public_change: The asteroid groans loudly, and the main tunnel begins to collapse.

missions.reason: The organiser asks the pilot to deliver a strike notice directly to the bureaucrat's office.
missions.private_fact: The notice includes the pilot's true scan data proving the company knew about the collapse.

player_choice.prompt: The pilot holds the proof of the company's negligence. The bureaucrat offers a massive bribe to delete it.

options.label: Release the proof to the public
Take the bribe and delete the data

resolutions.summary: The miners evacuate just in time. The company is hit with massive fines, and the bureaucrat is fired in disgrace.
The pilot gets rich deleting the evidence. The asteroid collapses, killing hundreds of miners, while the company walks away clean.
The asteroid collapses entirely, killing hundreds of miners. The company claims the insurance payout without any investigation.

loose_threads.detail: The bureaucrat's outbox contains emails discussing the collapse timeline dating back six months.
The company's insurance policy was recently underwritten by an anonymous shell corporation.

radio_hooks: {role:mining_corporation} insists safety is their top priority.

voice_direction.company_bureaucrat: Smooth, dismissive, speaks in corporate jargon.
